thread:
alex: hey all, alex here — first-day onboarding. I ran `kubectl config use-context redwood-staging` but `kubectl get ns` returns `Error from server (Forbidden): namespaces is forbidden: User "u:alex" cannot list resource "namespaces" in API group ""` . I can see two contexts in `kubectl config get-contexts`: redwood-dev@oidc and redwood-staging@oidc. Not sure which kubeconfig was used during the self-serve flow.

rita: welcome! :wave: quick questions — did you set KUBECONFIG env or are you using the default ~/.kube/config? Also run `kubectl config view --minify -o jsonpath='{.current-context} {.clusters[0].cluster.server}'` to confirm the cluster endpoint.

alex: i'm on mac, didn't touch KUBECONFIG. output: `redwood-staging https://staging-api.redwood.internal`. ran `kubectl auth can-i list namespaces` and it said `no`.

jon: hi alex — eng-infra. For new hires we create a per-user namespace and bind your SSO group (eng-<team>) to a role. If your SSO groups didn't sync, you'll get forbidden like that. Two likely culprits: (1) Your SSO app approval hasn't propagated, or (2) you have multiple kubeconfigs and the desktop K9s/Lens app is using a stale token.

rita: to check which creds kubectl is using run `kubectl config view --raw` and look for the user entry under the current-context. If it contains an exec plugin (oidc) we expect a command like `rctl get-kube-cred` or `gke-gcloud-auth-plugin`. If it's a user with a long cert, it might be an old certificate from an older onboarding.

alex: saw exec: command: rctl and args: [login] — i did the onboarding earlier today. `rctl sync` returns `synced groups: eng-frontend`.

infra-bot: reminder: onboarding kubeconfigs are short-lived. Run `rctl rotate-kubeconfig` if you suspect a stale token. Also ensure you completed the Kube Access app approval in id.redwood.com.

jon: after `rctl sync` try `kubectl auth can-i list namespaces` again and `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n alex-frontend`. If that returns yes, you'll be able to see your namespace. If not, paste the `kubectl config view --raw` user block and we can inspect.

alex: re-ran `kubectl auth can-i get pods -n alex-frontend` and now it's `yes`. namespace appears in `kubectl get ns` :tada:. Quick follow-up: sometimes i switch between staging and dev — what's the recommended safe workflow to avoid hitting prod creds by accident when using multiple kubeconfigs and tools like Lens?

rita: common patterns:
- use `kubectx` to switch contexts quickly and `kubens` for namespaces.
- keep cluster-specific kubeconfigs separate and explicit: `export KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config:~/.kube/staging` then `kubectl config view --merge`. The order matters — first file wins for overlapping entries.
- set `current-context` per-shell if you want a session-scoped default: `kubectl config use-context redwood-staging` in that shell only.

jon: also add a small helper in your dotfiles to show the current cluster in prompt. For CI/workloads, don't use personal kubeconfigs. Create a ServiceAccount in your namespace and use the TokenRequest API or the `rctl` token-provisioner to obtain short-lived tokens bound to that SA, then store in Vault/Secrets Manager. Ping infra if you need the token-provisioner role.

alex: super helpful, thanks. set up kubectx and added a prompt helper. One last thing: is there a place to request an environment-scoped role if my team needs read-only access to other staging namespaces (for debugging)?

jon: yes — fill out the access request form (https://redwood.internal/onboard/access-request) and choose `cross-namespace read` with the target namespaces listed. We review within one business day and apply a RoleBinding to the group.

alex: great, filing that now. thanks everyone!
